subject: Architecture
title: The Pentagon: The World's Largest Office
description: A quick win: understand The Pentagon: The World's Largest Office.

hook.text: The Pentagon has 17.5 miles of corridors but you can walk between any two points in 7 minutes.

buildup.text: It was built in just 16 months during World War II — one of the fastest major constructions ever.

discovery.text: Its five-sided shape wasn't symbolic. It was designed to fit an irregular plot of land.

twist.text: It has twice as many bathrooms as needed — it was built during segregation with separate facilities.

climax.text: The building houses 23,000 workers and has its own zip code, fire department, and shopping mall.

punchline.text: A building so big it's basically a small city with five walls.

quiz.question: Why does the Pentagon have an unusual number of bathrooms?
options: To handle emergency situations during wartime
It was built during segregation with separate facilities
To accommodate its shopping mall visitors

details.summary: The Pentagon in Arlington, Virginia, is the world's largest office building by floor area — 620,000 square meters housing 23,000 workers. Despite its enormous size.
details.whyItMatters: The Pentagon's five-ring design solves the fundamental problem of large building sizes — how to keep distances walkable. Its efficient layout allows 23,000 people to reach any point in minutes, a circulation solution that remains unmatched.
takeaways: World's largest office building at 620,000 square meters
23,000 workers can walk between any two points in seven minutes
Five concentric rings with connecting corridors maximize efficiency

faq.question: Why is the Pentagon shaped like a pentagon?
faq.answer: The original site was bordered by five roads, so architect George Bergstrom designed a five-sided building to fit. When the site changed, the five-sided design was kept because it proved efficient. Roosevelt approved it partly because pentagon geometry maximized interior usable space.

faq.question: How fast was the Pentagon built?
faq.answer: Construction took just 16 months from September 1941 to January 1943, with workers occupying completed sections while the rest was still being built. Up to 15,000 construction workers labored in shifts during wartime urgency. It remains one of the fastest large-building constructions in history.
